title: Rav Shimi bar Chiya bar Rav
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He had the privilege of receiving teaching from his grandfather Rav and attending upon him.

He raised difficulties before Rav, as in [Yoma 28b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.28b.9) and [Niddah 14a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.14a.11). In [Yevamot 45a:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.45a.14) he said to Rav: “But people say: ‘A camel in Media dances on a kab.’” In [Kiddushin 12a:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.12a.14) he sat before Rav.

Hyman cites Avodah Zarah 57 and Bekhorot 45a for Shimi’s objections to Rav. In [Menachot 29a:3-4](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.29a.3-4) and 110, and [Bekhorot 43b:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.43b.16), he raised an objection to Rav, and Rav said to him: “Are you Rav Shimi?” (Rashi explains: “You are Shimi, a great scholar, and you raise this difficulty against me.” Some say that Rav did not raise his eyes; in [Niddah 24a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.24a.15) this interpretation is rejected.)[^1][^5][^6]
In [Shabbat 111a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.111a.9) he spoke in Rav’s name, and in [Bava Metzia 73a:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.73a.8) he said: “And Rav concedes,” etc.

In [Berakhot 47a:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.47a.12): “Rav and Shmuel were sitting at a meal. Rav Shimi bar Chiya came and was hastening (hurrying) and eating. Rav said to him: ‘What is your reasoning?’” etc.
In [Chullin 111b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.111b.14): “Rav happened to come to the house of Rav Shimi bar Chiya, his son’s son. His eyes were sore, and they prepared an ointment for him.”[^2]
“From all this,” Hyman concludes, “we see that he was already a great scholar of his generation even during Rav’s lifetime.”

He is also mentioned in [Shabbat 139b:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.139b.14), where he said: “Provided that he does not make a hollow.” In [Eruvin 30a:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.30a.7) he said: “One may establish an eruv with raw eggs.” In [Yevamot 59b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.59b.6) he said: “A woman who has had intercourse with an animal remains eligible to marry a priest.”[^3][^4]

notes.text: Translated from Hyman, volume 3, printed page 1115 (scan page 282). The small-type parenthesis is read as ד״ז (“this matter”) and כד. (24a); earlier uncertain readings are documented in the proofreading record. The printed comma-like marks after נז and קי do not securely specify an amud, so Avodah Zarah 57 and Menachot 110 are cited without adding one. The remaining references follow the printed locators; they have not all been independently collated.

The named William Davidson Chullin 111b text explicitly calls Rav Shimi bar Chiya Rav’s son’s son and describes Rav’s eye complaint and the preparation of an ointment. Hyman’s further conclusion that Shimi was already a great scholar in Rav’s lifetime remains his inference.
The Hebrew preserves the printed ממהר (“hurrying”), הוו and אקבא rather than silently normalizing them. The legal statements and questions are translated as they appear in Hyman’s article.

Chullin explicitly calls Shimi Rav’s grandson. Shabbat transmits a ruling in Rav’s name through Shimi. Heilprin’s parallel entry records the alternative explanations for Rav’s question and gives a different Chullin folio. See [Heilprin’s parallel notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3297&lang=en).

Rav’s “Shimi, is that you?” appears in the dispute over the height of the menorah in Menachot, and in the discussion of a crooked spine in Bekhorot 43b. In Berakhot, Rav questions whether Shimi can join the meal and Shmuel replies.

The exchange checked at [Bekhorot 43b:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.43b.16) concerns the expression “two spines.” Shimi challenges Rav, who explains that the spine is crooked. The separate objection cited at Bekhorot 45a remains unverified.
